Let \(S\) be the set of all \(3\)-cycles in \(A_5\). Since \(S\) is a conjugacy class and is closed under inverse, the distance satisfies
\[
d(\sigma,\tau)=\ell(\sigma^{-1}\tau),
\]
where \(\ell(g)\) is the word length of \(g\) with respect to \(S\).

The conjugacy classes of \(A_5\) have sizes
\[
1,\quad 20,\quad 15,\quad 12,\quad 12,
\]
corresponding to
\[
e,\quad 3\text{-cycles},\quad (2,2)\text{-cycles},\quad 5A,\quad 5B.
\]
Every nonidentity element has distance \(1\) or \(2\): \(3\)-cycles have distance \(1\), and the other classes have distance \(2\). For example,
\[
(abc)(adc)=(ad)(bc),\qquad (abc)(cde)=(abcde),
\]
so double transpositions and \(5\)-cycles are products of two \(3\)-cycles. Thus the kernel
\[
K_p(g)=d(e,g)^p
\]
has class values
\[
0,\quad 1,\quad 2^p,\quad 2^p,\quad 2^p.
\]

Because \(K_p\) is central, convolution by \(K_p\) acts by scalars on irreducible \(A_5\)-isotypic components. The character table values needed are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
 & e & 3A & 2A & 5A & 5B\\
\hline
\chi_1 & 1&1&1&1&1\\
\chi_3 & 3&0&-1&\phi&\bar\phi\\
\chi_{3'}&3&0&-1&\bar\phi&\phi\\
\chi_4&4&1&0&-1&-1\\
\chi_5&5&-1&1&0&0
\end{array}
\]
where \(\phi+\bar\phi=1\).

For an irreducible character \(\chi\) of degree \(m\), the convolution eigenvalue is
\[
\lambda_\chi=\frac1m\sum_{g\in A_5}K_p(g)\chi(g).
\]
Let \(a=2^p\). For the nontrivial irreducibles:

\[
\lambda_3=\lambda_{3'}=\frac{a(-15+12)}3=-a,
\]
\[
\lambda_4=\frac{20-24a}{4}=5-6a,
\]
\[
\lambda_5=\frac{-20+15a}{5}=-4+3a.
\]

Negative type on the zero-sum subspace is equivalent to all nontrivial eigenvalues being \(\le 0\). Since \(a=2^p>1\), the first three are already negative, and the only condition is
\[
-4+3a\le 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
2^p\le \frac43.
\]
Hence
\[
\wp=\log_2\frac43.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), the only zero eigenvalue is on the irreducible component of degree \(5\). Its isotypic component in the real group algebra has dimension
\[
5^2=25.
\]
The constant component is excluded by \(\sum_\sigma c_\sigma=0\), so
\[
\dim E=25.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\log_2\frac43,\ 25\right)}
\]
